_readme:
The services register — what each shop STATES it can do, in its own words, with the source and the date somebody read it. Same discipline as data/curated/elephants.json: a row is a shop's own claim, never the ants' opinion, and 'unstated' is a value meaning the pages read did not say — it is not a no. Nothing here ranks one shop against another, and nothing here sorts shops by who their customers look like.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. OpenStreetMap holds 371 hairdresser and beauty points across both provinces and not one of them carries a tag saying what the shop can do. Three tags exist at all — male, female, unisex, on 29 shops between them — and WO-22 lifted those into the facet row. Everything a person actually wants to know (does anyone here cut tightly coiled hair, do you braid, do you have a digital perm machine, will you come to my hotel) has no tag, no register, and no crawl. It is stated by the shop or it is not known. audit_beauty.py proved the other half of this: across all 18,686 records in the catalogue, ZERO names say perm, updo, afro, textured or house call. There is no name rule waiting to be written. This file, an owner ticking their own facets, and a walk down the soi are the only three ways any of it is ever answered.

Fields per shop: `place` (record id), `stated` (facet key -> yes | unstated, exactly the keys in the `beauty` set of data/facets.json), `prices_th`/`prices_en` as posted, `note_th`/`note_en`, `source`, `fetched`, `stated_by`. A shop that was read and said nothing about a service gets `unstated`, which is how the page can tell 'we asked and it was silent' from 'nobody has looked'.
_doors: Nothing in `shops` yet, and that is the true state, not an oversight — no shop's own page has been read, because reading them is network work and WO-22's build was zero-network. The queue is ready: 18 beauty records already carry a website, a Facebook page or a LINE link, and they are the first 18 reads the moment Nan says go. See notes/beauty-proposal-2026-08-20.md for the numbered doors.
